description: calibration.py in sandbox_executor is one 1,637-line module. parse_actual_metrics is about 226 lines with cyclomatic complexity 61 and carries a noqa suppression. generate_calibration, resolve_git_ref, parse_predicted_metrics, run_calibrate and compute_calibration_deltas each exceed the complexity limits, and flow/stages/calibrate.py holds a run_calibrate_stage of complexity 27. Predicted-metric extraction, actual-metric extraction, delta computation, report rendering and the I/O shell are mixed in one file, so each change to a metric touches the same oversized function.
goal: Convert sandbox_executor/calibration.py into a calibration package with these modules: predicted.py (PredictedMetrics.from_plan), actual.py (ActualMetrics.from_execution), deltas.py (pure delta computation), report.py (report rendering) and run.py (the I/O shell that reads ledgers and git and writes the report). calibration/__init__.py re-exports the public names previously importable from sandbox_executor.calibration, so existing importers keep working. Replace the single parse_actual_metrics branch chain with a table of small per-metric extractors. Decompose resolve_git_ref, parse_predicted_metrics, generate_calibration, run_calibrate and compute_calibration_deltas so each function meets the repository's complexity and line budgets. flow/stages/calibrate.py delegates to calibration.run and keeps its behaviour. Split tests/test_calibration.py along the same module boundaries. Generated calibration reports must be byte-identical to the current output on the existing fixtures. Keep the change to a refactor: no behaviour changes. Module line budgets (holon-config/hygiene/module_budgets.json) are frozen: never change that file; if a module would exceed its limit, split it further.
rationale: Metric parsing is the most complex function in the calibration path and is the place every new metric lands. Separating the pure delta and report logic from the ledger and git I/O makes each part testable without a running flow and removes the noqa suppression.
acceptance_criteria: sandbox_executor.calibration keeps every public name it exported before the split, and existing imports still resolve.
parse_actual_metrics no longer exists as a single branch chain; metric extraction uses a table of small per-metric extractors, and no noqa suppression remains for complexity on these functions.
Each function in the calibration package and flow/stages/calibrate.py meets the repository complexity and line budgets without exemption.
Calibration reports for the existing fixtures are byte-identical to the output before the split.
All tests pass via 'uv run pytest', and 'uv run task lint' and 'uv run task lint-docs' pass.
